altar_tuff.source: Street altars for offerings, tuff with pulvini

amphora_group.source: Transport amphorae leaning by shop doors and stalls

bench_marble_exedra.source: Curved public seat (schola) with lion-paw ends, a form known from Pompeian tomb benches

bench_tuff.source: Masonry benches against house fronts, as at Pompeii

bench_wood.source: Plain timber benches outside houses and shops

bollard_basalt.source: Kerb-side guard stones protecting corners and fountains from cart wheels

cart_plaustrum.source: Two-wheeled ox cart (plaustrum) with solid wheels

cippus_amphitheatre.source: Travertine boundary stones around the amphitheatre pavement (five in situ on the east side), with sockets for barriers

columna_rostrata.source: Rostral column in the manner of the column of C. Duilius (260 BC): shaft with ship's beaks, statue on top

compital_shrine_imperial.source: Lares Augusti after the reorganisation of the vici in 7 BC; marble aedicula with altar

compital_shrine_republic.source: Crossroads shrines of the Lares Compitales (Compitalia); painted masonry aedicula with altar

dipinto_0.source: Painted wall notices: electoral programmata in red or black and edicta munerum announcing gladiator shows (Pompeii)

dipinto_1.source: Painted wall notices: electoral programmata in red or black and edicta munerum announcing gladiator shows (Pompeii)

dipinto_2.source: Painted wall notices: electoral programmata in red or black and edicta munerum announcing gladiator shows (Pompeii)

dolium.source: Large storage jar (dolium) for wine, oil or grain

drain_grate.source: Stone drain cover with slots over the street sewer; gutters lead rainwater from the pavement

garland_swag.source: Festival garlands (serta) of leaves and ribbons hung between posts and across doorways

honorific_column_imperial.source: Marble honorific column with gilded bronze statue

lacus_imperial.source: Agrippa's programme of 33 BC: 700 lacus and 500 salientes (Pliny, NH 36.121)

lacus_republic.source: Public basins (lacus) fed by the republican aqueducts; slab basin with spout stone as catalogued at Pompeii

meta_sudans.source: Flavian conical fountain beside the amphitheatre, Domitianic (c. AD 89-96); about 17 m high, basin about 16 m wide

milestone_imperial.source: Imperial milestones with the emperor's titulature, numerals picked out in red

milestone_republic.source: Cylindrical milestones on the roads from the 2nd century BC; about 1.5 m high, 0.5 m diameter, square base

portico_bay_imperial.source: Colonnaded portico (porticus) with travertine columns, architrave and tiled roof, giving shade along a piazza

portico_bay_republic.source: Timber-posted lean-to portico with tiled roof shading shop fronts

shop_awning.source: Cloth awnings and projecting timber lean-tos (pergulae, maeniana) over shop fronts

shop_shutter.source: Taberna front: grooved threshold with vertical plank shutters and a night door

shop_sign_0.source: Painted shop signs on boards and plaster panels

shop_sign_1.source: Painted shop signs on boards and plaster panels

shop_sign_2.source: Painted shop signs on boards and plaster panels

shrub_laurel.source: Bay laurel (Laurus nobilis) and myrtle as low planting

stall_masonry_0.source: Vendor stalls with plastered, painted counters (imperial tabernae and thermopolia)

stall_masonry_1.source: Vendor stalls with plastered, painted counters (imperial tabernae and thermopolia)

stall_masonry_2.source: Vendor stalls with plastered, painted counters (imperial tabernae and thermopolia)

stall_wood_0.source: Trestle stalls of street vendors under cloth awnings

stall_wood_1.source: Trestle stalls of street vendors under cloth awnings

stall_wood_2.source: Trestle stalls of street vendors under cloth awnings

statue_bronze_0.source: Honorific bronze statues on tuff bases in public places of the late Republic

statue_bronze_1.source: Honorific bronze statues on tuff bases in public places of the late Republic

statue_bronze_2.source: Honorific bronze statues on tuff bases in public places of the late Republic

statue_bronze_3.source: Honorific bronze statues on tuff bases in public places of the late Republic

statue_marble_0.source: Marble statues on inscribed, moulded bases

statue_marble_1.source: Marble statues on inscribed, moulded bases

statue_marble_2.source: Marble statues on inscribed, moulded bases

statue_marble_3.source: Marble statues on inscribed, moulded bases

stepping_stones.source: Raised crossing stones between the kerbs; attested at Pompeii, used here for the unpaved-to-silex streets of the Republic

sundial_column.source: Public sundial (hemicyclium) on a column; Rome had public dials from the 3rd century BC

thermopolium_counter.source: L-shaped masonry bar counter with embedded dolia, marble-faced (Pompeii, Herculaneum, Ostia)

torch_post.source: Free-standing cresset for festivals and night watch; regular street lighting is not attested

tree_cypress.source: Mediterranean cypress (Cupressus sempervirens), common by sanctuaries and tombs

tree_stone_pine.source: Umbrella pine (Pinus pinea), planted in Rome since the Republic
